'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[War in Donbas (2014–2022)|War in Donbas]]
***[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] rules out deploying [[United States Army|American troops]] unilaterally to [[Ukraine]] in order to deter a potential [[Russia]]n invasion, saying that the option "was not on the table". '''Arts and culture'''
*The bones of over 100 [[Indigenous Australians|Indigenous Australian]] [[Kaurna]] people are [[Repatriation and reburial of human remains|repatriated]] from the [[South Australian Museum]] and buried in a ceremony in [[Adelaide]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/dec/08/this-is-what-we-need-indigenous-remains-finally-laid-to-rest-in-historic-adelaide-ceremony (''The Guardian'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Indian Air Force Mil Mi-17 crash]]
**[[Chief of Defence Staff (India)|Chief of Defence Staff]] [[Bipin Rawat]] and 12 other people are killed when their [[Indian Air Force]] [[Mil Mi-17|Mi-17V-5]] crashes near [[Coonoor]], [[Tamil Nadu]], while flying from [[Sulur Air Force Station]] to [[Wellington, Tamil Nadu|Wellington]]. Another person was injured. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-59576082 (BBC News)]
*[[2021 Semeru eruption]]
**The death toll from the eruption of the [[Semeru]] volcano in [[Indonesia]] increases to 39. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20211208-death-toll-from-indonesia-volcano-eruption-rises-to-39 (France 24)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]], [[COVID-19 drug development]]
****[[China]]'s [[National Medical Products Administration]] approves the use of the neutralizing antibody cocktail developed by BRII Biosciences to treat [[COVID-19]] in adults and teenagers. [https://financialpost.com/pmn/business-pmn/china-approves-brii-biosciences-covid-19-treatment (''Financial Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in India]]
****[[India]]'s [[Serum Institute of India|Serum Institute]] announces that it will halve the production of its [[COVID-19 vaccine]] because it has no new orders for the vaccine. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-59574878 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kuwait]]
****[[Kuwait]] reports its first case of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant]] in a fully vaccinated European citizen who travelled from an African country. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/latest-on-coronavirus-outbreak/kuwait-records-first-case-of-omicron-variant/2442301# (Anadolu Agency)] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[South Korea]] reports a record 7,175 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 489,484. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2021/12/08/asia-pacific/south-korea-covid-surge/ (''The Japan Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in England]]
*****[[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|British Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]] announces new "Plan B" restrictions that include working from home for those who can beginning on December 13, and an extension of mandatory [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|face mask]] wearing to more indoor venues beginning on December 10. The restrictions also include usage of the mandatory NHS COVID pass in order to enter nightclubs and other venues with large crowds, as well as daily tests for people who had contact with a person who tested positive for the Omicron variant. [https://news.sky.com/story/covid-19-boris-johnson-announces-plan-b-restrictions-to-combat-spread-of-omicron-variant-12490130 (Sky News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark]]
****The [[Denmark|Danish]] [[Government of Denmark|government]] announces that schoolchildren will be sent home early from December 15 and nightlife establishments will close on December 10 due to persistently high number of COVID-19 cases. [https://www.dailysabah.com/world/europe/denmark-extends-holiday-break-for-schools-over-surging-infections (''Daily Sabah'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Romania]]
****[[Romania]] lifts its nighttime curfew and mandatory [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|outdoor face mask]] policy, allows shops and restaurants to close at 10 p.m. and allows entry to non-essential venues for those with a negative [[COVID-19 test]] as the number of cases declines. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/romanian-government-ease-some-covid-19-restrictions-2021-12-07/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in South Africa]]
***The [[South African Health Products Regulatory Authority]] approves the [[Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]] booster dose for people over the age of 18 that can be administered six months after their second dose, as well as [[immunocompromised]] people aged above 12 years that can be administered 28 days after their second dose. [https://businesstech.co.za/news/lifestyle/545320/south-africa-approves-pfizer-booster-shot-for-people-over-18-heres-when-you-should-take-it/amp/ (BusinessTech)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[1Malaysia Development Berhad scandal]]
**The [[Court of Appeal of Malaysia]] upholds the conviction against former [[Prime Minister of Malaysia|Prime Minister]] [[Najib Razak]] of all seven counts of [[abuse of power]], [[money laundering]] and [[Law of Malaysia|criminal breach of trust]] for his involvement in the 1MDB scandal. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/asia/malaysia-court-appeal-upholds-1mdb-najib-src-international-guilty-conviction-2363971 (CNA)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*Aftermath of [[2021 German federal election]]
**The [[Bundestag]] elects [[Olaf Scholz]] as the new [[Chancellor of Germany]], replacing [[Angela Merkel]] after 16 years in office. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-59575773 (BBC News)]

'''Sports'''

**[[Australia]], [[Canada]] and the [[United Kingdom]] join a [[United States|U.S.]]-led diplomatic [[boycott]] of the [[2022 Winter Olympics|upcoming Winter Olympic Games]] in [[Beijing]] citing [[China]]'s [[Uyghur genocide|human rights abuses]] in the [[Xinjiang]] region and [[Australia–China relations|Beijing's ongoing freeze on ministerial contact]] with [[Canberra]].
